description: A large oscilloscope that plots two signals against time or against each other, on a black panel you can widen to any size

params.text: Sets how far the first signal is magnified, in steps of a power of two from a quarter up to 256 times
Shifts the first signal before it is drawn, -10V to 10V added to it
Sets how far the second signal is magnified, in steps of a power of two from a quarter up to 256 times
Shifts the second signal before it is drawn, -10V to 10V added to it
Sets how long a stretch of signal the picture covers, 4 to 16, each step up halving it
Sets how fast the picture spins, -10 to 10

inputs.text: The first signal to plot; in Lissajous mode it is the horizontal axis, and in waveform mode it is drawn against time and is also the trigger
The second signal to plot; in Lissajous mode it is the vertical axis, and in waveform mode it is drawn against time
Sets the colour the trace is drawn in, 0-6V taking it once round the hue circle; with nothing patched the trace is drawn in the maker's orange
Lengthens the stretch of time the picture covers, doubling it for each volt
Adds to the rotation knob, one unit per volt

notes: drag either edge of the panel to make it wider or narrower; it will not go below 13HP.
in waveform mode the first signal is also the trigger: the drawing restarts when it rises past 1V, or after a tenth of a second if it does not.
menu: Lissajous mode — plots the first signal against the second instead of plotting both against time
Show statistics — prints the highest and lowest voltage held in each buffer above the picture

inputs.2:
0 to 6V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the maker's orange trace.
inputs.3:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
